text.text_excerpt: I stopped by the Cork & Bottle at the same time as the Mid City Green Market. They were having a wine tasting and the wines were mighty tasty. I was impressed with their stock & the sales people were helpful but not pushy. PLUS, they have their bourbon selection bottled by a company in Kentucky. How cool is that? And did I mention that it's a mighty tasty bourbon too.

I recently abandoned bikram yoga and have been able to fill that void by wandering the aisles of the wine store, aka my place of worship. I can spend hours meandering around, reading labels.....it's meditative. I want to give a shot out to my fave, Cork + Bottle, because they've earned it. My love for this place is based on the selection and, more so, the utter lack of pretension. I always have really good luck finding what I'm looking for at Cork + Bottle. Whenever I go through a phase (eg southern Italian whites) they've never failed to supply me with what I'm looking for. Case in point: one Friday afternoon I got a hankering for a dark n' stormy. Stopped in to buy cheese to go with the amazing loaf of bread I picked up at the green market (it's a wine store, they MUST sell cheese, right?) In general, this is a great place, huge selection of beers and wines, but I wouldn't recommend buying cheese there because no one really seems to know how it works. They've got a small selection (tasty stuff, though!) and it seems to be designed more for cheese plates people can order at Clever next door, and not so much for picking up a hunk of cheese to take home (like they have at Swirl).
